sentences.text: Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily, your host.
Today we visit Hue, a calm and historic city in Vietnam.
Hue is known for its beautiful river, old palaces, and peaceful atmosphere.
Let's explore this special Vietnamese city together.
Part 2 Where is Hue?
Hue is in the central part of Vietnam.
It is close to the Perfume River, a long and calm river that runs through the city.
The weather is warm, but it rains a lot in some seasons.
Hue is between mountains and the sea.
Part 3 History of Hue.
Hue was the old capital of Vietnam.
For many years, kings lived here.
There were palaces, temples, and royal gardens.
The history of Hue is very rich and important for Vietnamese culture.
Part 4 The Imperial City.
One of the most famous places in Hue is the Imperial City.
It is like a large old castle.
Inside, you can find gates, temples, and royal houses.
The colors red and gold are everywhere.
It shows the life of the kings long ago.
Part 5 The Perfume River.
The Perfume River is the heart of the city.
People take boat tours on the river.
At sunset, the light is beautiful and soft.
Along the river, there are parks, flowers, and walking paths.
Families and friends enjoy time together there.
Part 6 Food of Hue.
Food in Hue is famous for being small, pretty, and full of flavor.
A popular dish is Bun Ba Hue, a spicy noodle soup.
People also eat rice cakes, spring rolls, and sweet desserts.
Tea is very popular, especially lotus tea.
Part 7 Pagodas and Temples.
Hue has many peaceful pagodas.
The most famous one is Tien Mu Pagoda, a tall, beautiful tower by the river.
People come to pray, think, and enjoy the quiet place.
The sound of birds and water makes it relaxing.
Part 8 Daily Life in Hue.
Life in Hue is slow and calm.
People ride bicycles and motorbikes.
Markets open early in the morning.
Students wear white uniforms and go to school by bike.
In the evening, families eat together and enjoy fresh air outside.
Part 9 Traditional Clothes.
Vietnamese people sometimes wear Ao Dai, a long, elegant dress.
In Hue, many women wear Ao Dai for school or special days.
The dress is colorful and beautiful, showing Vietnamese culture.
Part 10 Nature Around Hue.
Near Hue, you can visit beaches, mountains, and green villages.
The area is great for walking and taking photos.
You can also visit old royal tombs, surrounded by trees and lakes.
Part 11 Festival's Hue has many traditional festivals.
The Hue Festival is the biggest.
People sing, dance, and show traditional art.
Visitors come from all over Vietnam and the world.
Part 12 Why Hue is Special.
Hue is special because it has peaceful river, old palaces, beautiful temples, colorful food, calm lifestyle, friendly people.
It is a perfect city for learning about Vietnam's history and culture.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
